the investigation of conduction mechanisms in boron doped epitaxial diamond layers.

boron doping level, activation energy, and capture cross section are not independent parameters, and they all depend on each other.
in boron doped diamond samples, the impurity band formation takes place at B/C ratio above 1000 ppm.

the boron activation energy decreases from 314 me V for low boron concentration down to 101meV for high boron concentration, and that the capture cross section for the boron dopant decreases with the increase of boron concentration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the boron acceptor in diamond is characterized by the following properties: (1) the impurity activation energy decreases with an increase in the boron concentration, (2) the impurity DOS becomes broader with increase of B/C, and (3) the capture cross section is reduced with an increase in B/C ratio.

the activation energy of boron in diamond is not a constant, but rather it varies in a wide range, from 314 to 101 mev, and the capture cross section is also not constant and varies from 3 x10 13 to 2 x10 17 cm 2.
the boron activation energy is not constant but it depends on the B/C ratio in the gas mixture and it is not equal to the boron ionization energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activation energy of conduction mechanism is not a fixed parameter, but it is a continuously varying quantity, which is determined by the doping concentration and temperature.
the activation energy of conduction in boron doped diamond can be continuously tuned in the wide temperature range 100-500 K.
the temperature dependence of admittance spectroscopy data is a powerful diagnostic tool for the investigation of conduction mechanisms in diamond samples.
